content.content:
The user wants list of South Asian countries and the name of the national anthems in English text (untranslated). So need to identify countries in South Asia. Typically South Asia includes: Afghanistan? Some definitions include Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka. Also sometimes includes Iran? No, usually South Asia region as per UN: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka. Also sometimes includes Tibet? Not a country. So we will list these eight countries. Provide anthem names in English (the official English titles). For each, provide the native name and English translation? The user wants English text (untranslated) meaning they want the anthem title in English (the common English name). Eg: India - "Jana Gana Mana". That's originally Sanskrit/Hindi but the title is in Sanskrit. In English we could give the title as "Jana Gana Mana". That's not translated. For Bangladesh: "Amar Shonar Bangla". For Pakistan: "Pak Sarzameen". Actually Pakistan's anthem is titled "Qaumi Tarana" but English name is "Pak Sarzameen". Usually it's "Pak Sarzameen". For Sri Lanka: "Sri Lanka Matha". For Nepal: "Sayaun Thunga Phoolka". For Bhutan: "Druk Tsenden". For Maldives: "Gaumii Salaam". For Afghanistan: "Milli Surood". Provide in English letters (transliteration). Provide maybe the English official translation? They ask "in english text (untranslated)". Probably they want the anthem name as used in English (the transliteration). So list.

Will produce answer.

content:
**South Asian Countries & Their National Anthems (English‑language titles – transliterated, not translated)**  

| # | Country | National Anthem (English‑language title) |
|---|---------|------------------------------------------|
| 1 | Afghanistan | **“Milli Surood”** (National Anthem) |
| 2 | Bangladesh | **“Amar Shonar Bangla”** (My Golden Bengal) |
| 3 | Bhutan | **“Druk Tsenden”** (The Thunder Dragon Kingdom) |
| 4 | India | **“Jana Gana Mana”** (Thou Art the Ruler of the Minds of All People) |
| 5 | Maldives | **“Gaumii Salaam”** (National Salute) |
| 6 | Nepal | **“Sayaun Thunga Phoolka”** (Made of Hundreds of Flowers) |
| 7 | Pakistan | **“Pak Sarzameen Shad Bash”** (May the Sacred Land of Pakistan Remain Happy) – commonly referred to simply as **“Qaumi Tarana”** (National Anthem) |
| 8 | Sri Lanka | **“Sri Lanka Matha”** (Mother Sri Lanka) |

**Notes**

* The titles are presented in the Roman alphabet exactly as they appear on official or widely‑used English‑language sources (i.e., they are *not* translated into English meaning).  
* Afghanistan’s anthem was adopted in 2007; Bangladesh’s was adopted in 1905 (later formalised as the national anthem in 1971).  
* Bhutan’s “Druk Tsenden” was adopted in 1953 and revised in 2007.  
* India’s “Jana Gana Mana” was adopted in 1950.  
* Maldives’ “Gaumii Salaam” became the anthem in 1972.  
* Nepal’s “Sayaun Thunga Phoolka” was adopted in 2007.  
* Pakistan’s anthem, composed in 1954 and officially adopted in 1954, is often identified by its opening line “Pak Sarzameen Shad Bash.”  
* Sri Lanka’s “Sri Lanka Matha” was adopted in 1951.  

These are the eight sovereign states that are generally classified as part of **South Asia** (as defined by the United Nations and most regional groupings) and the official names of their national anthems in English‑language transliteration.
